pages.title: Bus rapid transit
pages.content:
Bus rapid transit corridors with dedicated lanes cut average travel times by roughly 30 percent compared with mixed traffic in the surveyed cities.

Stations with level boarding and off-board fare payment reduced dwell time to under 20 seconds per stop.

Capital cost per kilometre was about 9 million dollars, far below light rail.

pages.title: Light rail
pages.content:
Light rail lines carry between 10,000 and 20,000 passengers per hour per direction at peak.

Construction cost averaged 60 million dollars per kilometre in the sampled projects.

Lines are expected to operate for at least 50 years with scheduled renewal of track and vehicles.

pages.title: Fare policy
pages.content:
Fare-free pilots in three mid-sized cities raised weekday ridership by 20 to 35 percent in the first year.

Operating subsidies had to grow by about 15 percent to cover the lost fare revenue.

Surveys found that a share of new riders were former walkers and cyclists rather than former drivers.

pages.title: Fare policy notes (2022)
pages.content:
Fare-free pilots raised weekday ridership by about 8 percent in the first year.

Operating subsidies rose by roughly 15 percent to replace fare revenue.

pages.title: Electric buses
pages.content:
Battery-electric buses reduced fuel and maintenance spending by about 40 percent per kilometre in depot trials.

Winter range fell by up to 25 percent when cabin heating relied on the battery.

Overnight depot charging was sufficient for routes under 200 kilometres a day.

pages.title: Electric buses in service
pages.content:
In field service, battery-electric buses reduced fuel and maintenance spending by about 22 percent per kilometre.

Drivers reported smoother acceleration and lower cabin noise.

pages.title: Bike lanes
pages.content:
Protected bike lanes were linked to a 28 percent drop in cyclist injuries on treated streets.

Painted lanes without physical separation showed no measurable change in injury rates.

Lane continuity across intersections mattered more than lane width.

pages.title: Congestion pricing
pages.content:
A cordon charge of 15 dollars reduced vehicle entries into the central zone by 18 percent.

Revenue was earmarked for transit improvements.

Public support rose after the first year once travel times improved.

pages.title: Congestion pricing critique
pages.content:
Critics argued that a cordon charge pushes traffic onto neighbouring streets.

Monitoring found no increase in traffic on the surrounding streets after the charge.

pages.title: Transit-oriented development
pages.content:
Housing built within 800 metres of a station generated 2.3 times more trips by transit than comparable housing elsewhere.

Parking minimums were removed in the study districts.

Retail vacancy near stations stayed below the regional average.

pages.title: Parking policy
pages.content:
Parking minimums were not removed in the study districts.

Curbside pricing was introduced on the busiest commercial streets.

pages.title: Accessibility
pages.content:
Only 54 percent of bus stops in the audited network met step-free access standards.

Audible announcements were present on all rail vehicles but only on a minority of buses.

Complaints about missing ramps fell by half after the retrofit programme.

pages.title: Accessibility audit (2020)
pages.content: Only 31 percent of bus stops in the audited network met step-free access standards.

pages.title: Ridership recovery
pages.content:
Weekday ridership recovered to 87 percent of the 2019 level by the end of 2025.

Weekend ridership exceeded its 2019 level.

Peak-hour crowding remained below pre-pandemic levels on most lines.

pages.title: Regional ridership recovery
pages.content:
Weekday ridership in the region reached 92 percent of the 2019 level by the end of 2025.

Commuter rail recovered faster than urban bus services.

pages.title: Signal priority
pages.content:
Transit signal priority shortened bus journey times by 6 to 10 percent on equipped corridors.

Benefits were largest where signals were close together.

Emergency vehicle pre-emption always overrides priority requests.

pages.title: Maintenance costs
pages.content:
Annual maintenance for a bus averages 28,000 dollars.

Rail vehicle maintenance is typically cheaper per passenger-kilometre than bus maintenance.

Deferred maintenance raised failure rates by 12 percent within two years.

pages.title: Rail economics
pages.content:
Rail vehicle maintenance is typically more expensive per passenger-kilometre than bus maintenance.

Fixed infrastructure costs dominate the budget of rail operators.
